messages:
maria: heads-up — nightly perf run shows a regression on SM90 when using Triton flash variants with paged KV. tokens/sec down ~18% at seq=4096 compared to last week. commit: 5f2d8a3

aj: ugh, any idea which layer? kernel selection, batching, or KV fallback?

maria: initial profiler points to higher L2 traffic and increased kernel launches. p50 latency went from 42ms -> 51ms for chunked attention steps.

ken: can you paste the run command and the model config?

maria: sure — running locally on sm90 instance:
```
./bench --model=gptx-3b --seq=4096 --bs=1 --kv-paged=true --attn=flash2-triton --cuda=15.2 --warm=10 --iters=100
```

riley: note we recently changed the kernel selector to prefer Triton for flash2 when sm>=90 (PR 4387). might be hitting a codegen regression in Triton for our block size.

aj: perf-bot, can you attach the perf diff for the nightly?

perf-bot: nightly/17684: flash2-triton (sm90) tokens/sec -18.2% vs baseline(17612). regression appears only for seq>=2048 and when paged KV is enabled.

maria: attaching a tiny profiler snippet:
```
[profile] kernel: flash2_triton_attn  calls=512 avg_ms=0.98 l2_bytes=1.2GB
[kv] page-loads/sec=34 stall_ms=12
[kern] extra-launches=64
```

ken: extra-launches smells like we lost a fused kernel path and Triton is launching small kernels per head. did selector fallback to per-head kernels?

maria: selector.log shows chosen_variant=triton_flash2_shard_unk and fallback=false. but CUDA kernel timeline shows many small launches at different grid sizes.

riley: can you repro with native cuda flash (non-triton) for comparison?

maria: yes — running same args with --attn=flash2-cuda: tokens/sec +12% vs triton on the same machine.

aj: OK this isolates to Triton codegen path. next steps: 1) bisect Triton commit range used in our deploy image, 2) run microbench per-blocksize to see where launch counts spike, 3) confirm not a driver/CUDA 15 scheduling change.

ken: I'll start a narrow bisect across triton wheel versions in our CI and post links. also add a synthetic that forces no-paged-kv to confirm interplay.

maria: also saw that with batching enabled (dynamic batching window=5) the regression shrinks to -8%. so batching hides part of the launch overhead. suggests batching heuristics can mitigate but not fix root cause.

riley: good to know. sounds like short-term mitigation is to prefer cuda kernels for seq>=2048 on SM90 if triton regression persists. can we add a transient selector rule with a flag?

aj: yes, add a temporary override in kernel_selector: if arch==sm90 and attn==flash2-triton and seq>=2048 and paged_kv==true then prefer flash2-cuda. tag it with TODO to remove after fix.

maria: created a small reproduce job: https://ci.internal/redwood/runs/176845/attn-triton-sm90-repro. please upvote if you can run it. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: queued bisect jobs for triton versions [2.1.0 .. 2.4.3]. ETA ~2h per step.

ken: added microbench script to repo: tools/perf/attn_launch_sleuth.sh — iterates block sizes and reports kernel launch count + time. please run on sm90 infra only.

aj: ACTIONS
- ken: run bisect and post first failing triton commit (by EOD)
- maria: add selector override PR and a note to ops playbook
- riley: coordinate rollback plan for dedicated if this hits prod

maria: I'll follow up with timeline & logs once bisect gives a commit. thanks all.
